requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Ordinary comments are excluded. Docstrings are source expressions and
participate in hashes along with the definition's other expressions.
rationale:
structural: I found no structural obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.python.fingerprints`, so it needs no implementation root. The requirement has no implementation edges and only test edges. I did not read the test sources, because test adequacy is outside this assessment. Each clause specifies observable behavior:

- "Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and whitespace-separated words": This fixes the digest value. An implementation could use a different SHA-256 library or a different hashing call path and produce identical digests, so the choice of library is discretionary. The encoding rules belong to the cited `requirements.references.structural_hash`, which this requirement only cites.
- "The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version": This only requires that the scheme string name the rules and their version. The `fingerprint_scheme` signature and the retention of the scheme in loaded contents are prescribed by the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`, so any structural obligation there belongs to that requirement. Here it is a cite and not an obligation of this text.
- "Ordinary comments are excluded. Docstrings are source expressions and participate in hashes along with the definition's other expressions.": These clauses state which text is hashed. An implementation could handle comments and docstrings through different mechanisms and still produce the same hashes. That is a behavioral obligation, and tests supply its evidence.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each observable obligation of `requirements.sdk.sources.python.fingerprints`.

- **SHA-256 digest:** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]` asserts the Python fingerprint is 64 hex characters. The encoding is unspecified, so a known-digest test isn't possible. The length and hex check is the reasonable observable check.
- **Whitespace-separated words:** in the same test, the Python case treats `"two words"` and `"two   words"` as equal. It treats `"twowords"` as different, so word boundaries are preserved.
- **Ordinary comments excluded:**
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile]` has a Python case with a leading comment and a trailing comment.
  - It checks that changing a comment's text, or removing the comments, leaves the hash unchanged.
  - It checks that a changed code word (`x` to `y`) changes the hash, so the exclusion is not simply ignoring everything.
  - The comment-and-whitespace Python case in `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` covers the same point.
- **Docstrings participate in hashes:** the docstring block in `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` checks two things. Whitespace-only reflow inside the docstring leaves the hash unchanged, which is the word rule. Changing the docstring words (`two words` to `changed words`) changes the hash, so the docstring is hashed and not treated as a comment.
- **Scheme identifies the rules and version:** `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` runs `check` with `languages::Python` and `python-structural-v1`. `check` asserts `language.fingerprint_scheme()`, `L::default().fingerprint_scheme()` and `inferred.fingerprint_scheme()` equal that value. Retention of the scheme in loaded contents belongs to the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`, so I did not reassess it here.
- **Decorators and attached structure:** `python_decorators_attach_to_the_decorated_definition_for_hashing` also checks that decorators affect the structural hash. This is context from the cited `requirements.references.structural_hash`, not an obligation of this requirement.

I found no behavior that the requirement's text requires and the tests would miss.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Ordinary comments are excluded. Docstrings are source expressions and
participate in hashes along with the definition's other expressions.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
